issues.description: SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(String,int,int) is specified as public in the UML (+acceptSupplyDelivery), but the reference solution declares it with package-private visibility (`static void acceptSupplyDelivery(...)`). Students following the UML will implement it as public, which can lead to API/visibility confusion and test failures if tests enforce the UML contract.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution method signature to `public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)` (or, if package-private is intended, update the UML/text to explicitly state non-public visibility).

issues.description: SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() is specified as public in the UML (+checkOrderReady), but the reference solution declares it with package-private visibility (`void checkOrderReady()`). This conflicts with the student-facing API in the statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method public in the solution: `public void checkOrderReady()`.

issues.description: The problem statement is internally inconsistent about whether SealSaloon.stock is static: the text explicitly requires `stock` to be static (shared across all instances), but the UML association line shows a non-static association/field named `stock` (no static marker). Students may be unsure whether to implement `stock` per-instance or shared.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the UML with the text by marking `stock` as static in the diagram (e.g., underline or `{static}`), and ensure the narrative consistently describes it as `static final` if it is meant to be shared.

issues.description: Stock exposes a public `setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[])` method in both template and solution, but this method is not present in the UML/API specification for Stock (which lists only add/take/find/addToStockIngredients/emptyStock). This extra public API contradicts the specified class interface and can mislead students about what methods they are expected/allowed to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Either add `setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[])` to the UML/spec as an intended method, or remove it from the template/solution and keep stock modification limited to the specified methods.
